source: Generic OBD-II diagnostic trouble codes as standardized by SAE J2012 / ISO 15031-6. Descriptions are the standard generic definitions; causes and checks are common-knowledge diagnostic guidance for the generic code, not manufacturer-specific procedures.
note: Manufacturer-specific codes (P1xxx, most B0xxx body codes, etc.) are intentionally excluded: their meaning varies by OEM and must be looked up in OEM service documentation.

possible_causes: Open or shorted actuator circuit wiring
recommended_checks: Inspect actuator solenoid connector and wiring
Check oil level and condition
Measure solenoid resistance against spec
Command the actuator with a scan tool and watch cam timing

codes.description: Intake (A) camshaft position timing over-advanced or system performance (bank 1)
possible_causes: Worn timing chain or incorrect timing
Continuous oil flow to the phaser
recommended_checks: Check oil level/viscosity and change if degraded
Swap or test the actuator solenoid
Compare commanded vs actual cam angle on live data
Verify timing chain alignment

codes.description: Crankshaft position - camshaft position correlation (bank 1 sensor A)
possible_causes: Oil control issues affecting the phaser
recommended_checks: Compare cam/crank sensor waveforms
Inspect timing chain, guides and tensioner
Check reluctor/tone wheels
Verify sensor air gaps and wiring

codes.description: Heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) heater control circuit (bank 1 sensor 1)
possible_causes: Open heater element in the O2 sensor
recommended_checks: Measure heater element resistance
Check heater circuit fuse and relay
Verify supply voltage at the sensor connector
Inspect harness routing for chafing

codes.description: Mass or volume air flow (MAF) circuit malfunction
possible_causes: Intake air leaks after the sensor
recommended_checks: Inspect and clean the MAF element with MAF cleaner
Check for intake leaks and loose ducting
Verify MAF signal and reference voltages
Compare MAF reading at idle/WOT with expected g/s

codes.description: Mass or volume air flow circuit range/performance
recommended_checks: Smoke-test the intake for leaks
Clean the MAF sensor
Verify volumetric efficiency from live data
Check air filter and intake path

codes.description: Mass or volume air flow circuit low input
recommended_checks: Confirm connector seating and pin tension
Measure signal voltage/frequency at idle
Check sensor power and ground
Wiggle-test the harness while watching live data

codes.description: Manifold absolute pressure (MAP)/barometric pressure circuit range/performance
possible_causes: Cracked or blocked vacuum hose to the sensor
recommended_checks: Compare MAP reading key-on-engine-off with barometric pressure
Inspect the sensor vacuum hose
Check for manifold vacuum leaks
Verify 5 V reference and ground

codes.description: Intake air temperature (IAT) sensor 1 circuit low input
recommended_checks: Compare IAT reading with ambient temperature
Measure sensor resistance vs temperature chart
Inspect wiring for shorts to ground

codes.description: Intake air temperature (IAT) sensor 1 circuit high input
recommended_checks: Check connector seating and pins
Measure circuit continuity to the ECM
Substitute a known-good sensor
Compare ECT vs IAT after cold soak (should match)
Verify warm-up rate against thermostat rating
Check coolant level and bleed air
Plot ECT during warm-up for dropouts

codes.description: Engine coolant temperature circuit low input
recommended_checks: Disconnect sensor: reading should jump to the cold limit
Measure sensor resistance vs temperature
Inspect wiring to the ECM

codes.description: Engine coolant temperature circuit high input
recommended_checks: Jumper the sensor connector: reading should go to the hot limit
Check continuity of both circuit wires
Inspect connector for corrosion

codes.description: Throttle/pedal position sensor A circuit range/performance
recommended_checks: Sweep the throttle slowly and watch for signal dropouts
Clean the throttle body
Verify TPS voltage at closed and wide-open throttle
Check 5 V reference and ground

codes.description: Coolant thermostat (coolant temperature below thermostat regulating temperature)
possible_causes: Thermostat stuck open or opening early
Very low ambient operation with light load
recommended_checks: Measure warm-up time vs specification
Verify thermostat opening temperature
Check fan control operation
Compare ECT against an infrared thermometer at the housing

codes.description: O2 sensor circuit low voltage (bank 1 sensor 1)
possible_causes: Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor
recommended_checks: Watch the sensor switch rich/lean on live data
Check fuel trims for a lean condition
Inspect exhaust manifold for leaks
Test sensor heater and signal wiring

codes.description: O2 sensor circuit slow response (bank 1 sensor 1)
recommended_checks: Measure sensor switching frequency at 2500 rpm
Inspect for exhaust leaks
Check for coolant or oil consumption
Replace sensor if response time is out of spec
Measure heater resistance cold
Verify battery voltage to the heater with key on
Check the heater circuit fuse

possible_causes: Low fuel pressure or weak pump
recommended_checks: Read long/short fuel trims at idle and cruise
Smoke-test intake and vacuum lines
Measure fuel pressure under load
Clean/test the MAF sensor
Check PCV system

possible_causes: Leaking injectors or high fuel pressure
recommended_checks: Check fuel trims
Inspect injectors for leak-down
Measure fuel pressure and regulator operation
Test the EVAP purge valve
Verify MAF readings

possible_causes: Same as P0171 but bank 2: vacuum leaks, MAF under-reporting, low fuel pressure
recommended_checks: If both P0171 and P0174 are set, suspect a common cause (MAF, fuel pressure, large vacuum leak) rather than per-bank components
Measure injector resistance
Check for injector pulse with a noid light
Inspect connector terminals
Swap injectors between cylinders to see if the code follows
Read misfire counters per cylinder
Inspect plugs and coils
Check fuel pressure and trims
Perform relative compression test
Smoke-test the intake

possible_causes: Faulty spark plug or coil on cylinder 1
recommended_checks: Swap coil and plug with another cylinder and see if the misfire follows
Test injector operation
Compression/leak-down test on cylinder 1

possible_causes: Faulty spark plug or coil on cylinder 2
recommended_checks: Swap coil/plug diagnostics as for P0301, applied to cylinder 2

possible_causes: Faulty spark plug or coil on cylinder 3
recommended_checks: Swap coil/plug diagnostics as for P0301, applied to cylinder 3

possible_causes: Faulty spark plug or coil on cylinder 4
recommended_checks: Swap coil/plug diagnostics as for P0301, applied to cylinder 4
Measure sensor resistance/output
Verify mounting torque
Inspect shielded wiring for damage
Watch knock retard on live data while tapping near the sensor

possible_causes: Harness damage near the crank pulley
recommended_checks: Scope the CKP signal while cranking
Inspect the tone wheel for damage/runout
Check connector and harness routing
Verify sensor air gap where adjustable
Scope CMP vs CKP signals
Check sensor supply/ground
Inspect trigger wheel
Verify timing marks
Command the EGR open at idle: engine should stumble
Clean EGR passages and valve
Test the EGR position/feedback sensor
Check vacuum lines and solenoid

possible_causes: Engine conditions (misfire, rich/lean) that damaged the catalyst
recommended_checks: Compare upstream vs downstream O2 waveforms
Check for stored misfire/fuel-trim codes first
Inspect for exhaust leaks
Measure catalyst temperature differential in/out
Diagnose as P0420 on bank 2; fix any misfire or mixture faults before condemning the converter
Check and reseat the fuel cap
Smoke-test the EVAP system
Actuate purge/vent valves with a scan tool
Inspect canister and lines
Smoke-test at low pressure to find small leaks
Verify cap seal condition
Check hose connections at the canister and tank
Confirm the fuel cap is present and sealing
Visually trace EVAP plumbing
Command the vent valve closed and test for pressure build
Compare scan-tool speed with actual speed
Scope the VSS signal while rolling
Inspect sensor and tone ring
Check for related ABS codes

possible_causes: Carboned throttle body / idle air passages
recommended_checks: Clean throttle body and IAC passages
Watch commanded vs actual idle rpm
Smoke-test for vacuum leaks
Test IAC/ETC operation with a scan tool
Load-test the battery
Measure charging voltage at idle with loads on
Inspect belt tension and condition
Voltage-drop test grounds and B+ cable

codes.description: Internal control module memory checksum error
recommended_checks: Check battery/charging system first
Attempt an ECM software update/reflash per OEM procedure
Replace the ECM only if the fault persists after reflash

possible_causes: Water intrusion in the ECM connector
recommended_checks: Inspect ECM power/ground circuits under load
Check for moisture/corrosion at the ECM
Reflash before replacement if supported

codes.description: Transmission control system malfunction (TCM has stored a code)
possible_causes: This code is informational: the TCM requested the MIL
Any transmission fault stored in the TCM
recommended_checks: Read codes from the TCM directly, not only the ECM
Diagnose the specific transmission code found there
Compare input and output speed sensor readings vs engine rpm
Measure sensor resistance
Inspect internal/external harness
Check ATF condition and level
Compare output speed with wheel speeds/VSS
Scope the sensor while driving
Inspect connector and harness

codes.description: Torque converter clutch circuit performance or stuck off
recommended_checks: Watch TCC slip rpm at steady cruise
Actuate the TCC solenoid with a scan tool
Check ATF level and condition
Inspect valve body if slip persists

codes.description: Left front wheel speed sensor circuit
possible_causes: Excessive air gap from hub/bearing wear
recommended_checks: Compare all four wheel speeds on a scan tool while rolling
Inspect the sensor, harness and tone ring
Measure sensor output (scope or AC voltage) while spinning the wheel
Check hub bearing play

codes.description: Right front wheel speed sensor circuit
possible_causes: Same failure modes as C0035, right front wheel
recommended_checks: Diagnose as C0035 on the right front corner

codes.description: Left rear wheel speed sensor circuit
possible_causes: Same failure modes as C0035, left rear wheel
recommended_checks: Diagnose as C0035 on the left rear corner

codes.description: Right rear wheel speed sensor circuit
possible_causes: Same failure modes as C0035, right rear wheel
recommended_checks: Diagnose as C0035 on the right rear corner

possible_causes: CAN_H/CAN_L wiring faults (open, short to power/ground, shorted together)
A failed node loading the bus
recommended_checks: Measure ~60 ohm between CAN_H and CAN_L with power off (two 120 ohm terminators)
Scope CAN_H/CAN_L for proper differential signalling
Unplug modules one at a time to find a bus-loading node
Inspect connectors and splices

codes.description: Control module communication bus A off
possible_causes: A module driving the bus into error (bus-off state)
recommended_checks: Check which module logged bus-off and when
Scope the bus during the fault if reproducible
Inspect harness sections that move (door hinges, engine-to-body)
Review error counters per node if the tool supports it

possible_causes: CAN wiring between ECM and gateway damaged
recommended_checks: Check ECM fuses and relays
Verify ECM wakes up and responds to a direct scan request
Measure CAN resistance and signals at the ECM connector
Check grounds for the ECM

codes.description: Lost communication with transmission control module (TCM)
recommended_checks: Diagnose as U0100 but at the TCM: fuses, grounds, CAN pins, direct response

codes.description: Lost communication with anti-lock brake system (ABS) control module
possible_causes: CAN wiring to the ABS module
recommended_checks: Check ABS fuses (often high-amp)
Verify the ABS module answers a direct request
Measure CAN signals at the ABS connector

codes.description: Lost communication with body control module (BCM)
recommended_checks: Check BCM fuses and grounds
Verify BCM communication directly
Inspect CAN wiring at the BCM

codes.description: Lost communication with instrument panel cluster (IPC) control module
recommended_checks: Check cluster fuses
Verify cluster communication directly
Inspect CAN wiring at the cluster connector

codes.description: Body system DTC family (airbags, seat belts, HVAC, lighting, etc.)
possible_causes: Note: unlike P0xxx codes, most body (B) codes in common use are manufacturer-specific; generic public definitions exist only for a small set
recommended_checks: Look body codes up in the OEM service documentation for the exact vehicle; do not rely on generic interpretations for airbag-related faults
